faq_heading: New construction in East Newton: your questions answered

faq.q: What have houses in East Newton sold for?

items.t: East Newton: 80 houses sold at a median of $1,382,500, with the middle half between $1,171,875 and $1,553,750. The median house took 38 days to sell and closed at 95.5% of list.
60 townhomes sold in East Newton at a median of $616,750 (middle half $557,425 to $699,925). A typical townhome in East Newton spent 36 days on the market and closed at 97.5% of the asking price.
In East Newton, condos sold at a median of $475,000 across 29 sales, and the middle half closed between $400,000 and $495,000. The median condo sat 32 days and sold for 97.0% of list.

blocks.text: Source: Paragon closed sales, November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026; medians need 5 or more sales.
How East Newton compares with the rest of Surrey

items.t: Houses in East Newton have the second highest median of 7 Surrey sub-areas, $1,382,500. Queen Mary Park Surrey is lowest at $1,178,500 and Sullivan Station highest at $1,397,200. Panorama Ridge ($1,380,000) sits just below and Sullivan Station ($1,397,200) sits just above.
Townhomes in East Newton have the lowest median of the 7 Surrey sub-areas, $616,750, below Queen Mary Park Surrey at $669,000; the highest is Panorama Ridge at $800,000.

Condos in East Newton have the second lowest median of 6 Surrey sub-areas, $475,000. Queen Mary Park Surrey is lowest at $436,500 and Sullivan Station highest at $574,000. Queen Mary Park Surrey ($436,500) sits just below and West Newton ($475,000) sits just above.

blocks.text: By build year, houses are the newest homes selling in East Newton (median 2002) and townhomes the oldest (median 1989), a gap of 13 years.
